biology.blood-data-graph.0002.a: Concentration rises after vaccination to a peak then falls (cannot read exact values without graph); quote data
biology.blood-data-graph.0002.b: Antigen in vaccine detected by lymphocytes; lymphocytes divide and secrete antibodies so concentration rises; antibodies then broken down / not produced once antigen removed so falls; memory cells remain

biology.blood-data-pct.0004.b: Pathogen infection; lymphocytes/phagocytes divide (mitosis) to produce more cells to fight pathogen; phagocytosis/antibody production

biology.blood-data-plot.0004.a: Axes labelled with units, time on x; sensible linear scale; points plotted correctly; smooth curve
biology.blood-data-plot.0004.b: Rises from 6 to a peak of 14 at day 3, then falls to 7 by day 6

biology.blood-data-read.0001.b: (value at 20 - value at 0)/20 au per day
biology.blood-data-read.0001.c: Lymphocytes produce antibodies in response to antigen, rise; then fall as antigen removed/antibodies broken down

biology.blood-describe.0003.all: Platelets exposed to air/damaged tissue release chemicals/enzymes; soluble fibrinogen converted to insoluble fibrin; fibrin forms mesh of fibres trapping red blood cells/platelets forming clot (scab)

biology.blood-describe-multi.0007.a: Prevents blood loss; prevents entry of pathogens
biology.blood-describe-multi.0007.b: Platelets release enzymes; fibrinogen to fibrin; mesh traps red blood cells

biology.blood-explain.0003.all: Antibodies are specific/complementary in shape to one antigen; different pathogen has different-shaped antigens so antibodies cannot bind

biology.blood-explain-multi.0006.b: Less oxygen in air / lower partial pressure at altitude; more red blood cells / haemoglobin to carry more oxygen; so enough oxygen reaches tissues for respiration

biology.blood-ext.0003.all: Biconcave shape - large SA:V for diffusion of oxygen; thin so short diffusion distance; no nucleus - more room for haemoglobin; haemoglobin binds oxygen forming oxyhaemoglobin in lungs, releases at tissues; small/flexible to pass through capillaries

biology.blood-mcq-rev.0004.all: Cell fragments involved in blood clotting

biology.blood-recall-multi.0001.a: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, plasma

biology.breeding-gm-describe.0004.all: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites to remove gene and open plasmid leaving sticky ends; ligase joins gene into plasmid (joins sugar-phosphate backbone) forming recombinant DNA

biology.breeding-gm-describe-multi.0007.b: Select parent plants with high yield; cross-breed them; select offspring with highest yield; repeat over many generations

biology.breeding-gm-explain.0004.all: Reduces genetic variation / inbreeding; increases chance of harmful recessive alleles being inherited together (homozygous) so genetic disorders; less resistance to disease; physical problems from exaggerated features

biology.breeding-gm-explain-multi.0002.b: Reproduce quickly so large amounts of protein produced fast; have plasmids / same genetic code so human gene expressed; few ethical issues/cheap to grow

biology.breeding-gm-ext.0002.all: Select cows with high milk yield and bulls from high-yield mothers; breed them; select offspring with highest milk yield; breed those; repeat over many generations; until all offspring produce high yield; mention variation, alleles, artificial insemination possible, reduced variation/inbreeding risk

biology.breeding-gm-mcq.0001.all: they can be made resistant to pests

biology.breeding-gm-mcq-rev.0007.all: Choosing parents with desired features to breed together

biology.breeding-gm-recall.0003.all: Inbreeding / reduced genetic variation leading to genetic disorders
